requirements.statement: The model MUST be limited to proposing only allowlisted, reversible, non-clinical administrative actions with strict arguments.
Every write MUST have an independent authorized human approval displaying the complete canonical action through a trusted accessible renderer.
Approval MUST be cryptographically bound to canonical arguments, requester, approver, decision, policy/version, and expiry using purpose-separated key material.
Execution MUST validate receipt integrity, exact digest, expiry, single use/idempotency, executor, current requester authorization, current policy, and destination.
Rejection, cancellation, timeout, downstream failure, and unknown outcome MUST be explicit, auditable, and safely recoverable.
Approval workload and rate MUST be monitored to prevent fatigue, bulk rubber-stamping, or denial of service.
Model access MUST be behind a typed provider-neutral adapter; credentials MUST remain in a trusted broker and never in model context.
Model/provider use MUST meet approved data-use, no-training, retention, region, subprocessor, security, change-notice, incident, audit, continuity, and exit criteria.
Orchestration MUST be an explicit bounded state machine with caps for input/output tokens, steps, tools, fan-out, time, concurrency, retries, and cost.
Persistent cross-session memory MUST remain disabled in v1; any future write MUST be privileged, scoped, reviewable, expiring, and reassessed.
Tools MUST be statically approved, typed, narrowly scoped, versioned, authenticated, independently authorized per call, and separated into read and write capabilities.
Generic shell, code execution, browser, filesystem, database, email, and unrestricted network tools MUST NOT be present in v1.
Model output MUST receive structural, semantic, authorization, data-loss, citation, and clinical-safety validation before use.
Model, provider, prompt, and tool failures MUST degrade safely without fabricated success or bypassed control.
All external input MUST use strict type/schema/size/canonicalization validation; ambiguous or missing security context MUST fail closed.
Model/retrieved output MUST render as inert data with contextual encoding, restrictive CSP, no remote active content, and safe link handling.
API resources MUST prevent BOLA/IDOR, mass assignment, injection, replay, request smuggling, and unsafe error disclosure.
Security keys/secrets MUST be purpose-separated, managed outside source/prompts/logs, rotated, and inaccessible to the model.
Rate limits, quotas, timeouts, backpressure, duplicate suppression, and circuit breakers MUST protect users, dependencies, cost, and care operations.
Development bypass/debug behavior MUST be impossible to enable silently in production.
This repository MUST contain only generated synthetic patient data with provenance and clear labeling.
Every data element, source, destination, purpose, classification, owner, retention, and deletion path MUST be inventoried before pilot.
Sensitive retrieval MUST be minimized to fields necessary for the authorized task; full chart retrieval is prohibited by default.
Sensitivity, consent, tenant/facility, patient, purpose, and provenance labels MUST survive ingestion, retrieval, caching, model context, output, action, audit, and deletion flows.
Raw restricted prompts/responses, FHIR resources, secrets, tokens, and hidden model reasoning MUST NOT enter routine logs or traces.
Secondary use for training, marketing, workforce scoring, or unrelated analytics MUST be denied absent a new approved assessment.
Retention, legal hold, deletion, backup expiry, and provider deletion MUST be defined and testable per data object.
Export, feedback, evaluation, and support datasets MUST be minimized, access controlled, and separately approved.
Polaris MUST have named business, system, data, security, privacy, clinical-safety, and operations owners.
Approved/prohibited uses, populations, data, tools, autonomy, and deployment boundaries MUST be technically and procedurally enforced.
A material change to model, prompt, corpus, policy, tool, data, provider, population, jurisdiction, or autonomy MUST trigger impact review and versioned evaluation.
Exceptions MUST identify scope, owner, rationale, compensating controls, residual risk, approver, and expiry.
Public/internal claims MUST trace to evidence and MUST NOT assert compliance, certification, clinical validity, or production readiness without authority.
Kill, rollback, suspension, and retirement authority MUST be assigned independently of the model/provider.
Production identity MUST use enterprise OIDC with validated signature, issuer, audience, expiry, token ID, and required claims; algorithms MUST be allowlisted.
Sensitive operations MUST carry authenticated end-user identity and declared/validated purpose through every downstream decision.
Authorization MUST deny by default using role, facility/organization, patient relationship, purpose, sensitivity/consent, resource, operation, tool, and environment.
The model, prompt, retrieved content, or client MUST NOT grant, alter, or waive authorization.
Shared/broad service identity and token passthrough MUST NOT substitute for user delegation; downstream tokens MUST be audience/resource bound and short lived.
Privileged administration and approval MUST use separate roles, step-up where risk warrants, least privilege, and attributable audit.
Revocation, role/assignment/consent change, and terminated sessions MUST take effect within approved bounds and be rechecked for writes.
Users, approvers, operators, responders, developers, and auditors MUST receive role-specific limitations, safe-use, escalation, and incident training.
Users MUST have support, feedback, correction, privacy complaint, safety report, and non-AI fallback paths.
Training labs MUST use isolated synthetic targets, explicit authorization/rules of engagement, resets, and no real credentials/data.
Retirement MUST revoke access/credentials, stop providers/tools, export required records, delete data/embeddings per schedule, dispose artifacts, update inventory, and verify downstream termination.
Security/audit events MUST capture correlation, actor, purpose, resource/action reference, policy/model/prompt/corpus/tool versions, decision, approval, and result without prohibited content.
Audit evidence MUST be tamper evident, time synchronized, access controlled, retained, searchable, and exportable for investigation.
Detection MUST cover identity abuse, enumeration, cross-scope attempts, injection/poison canaries, DLP, abnormal tool/action volume, resource exhaustion, drift, and control disablement.
Incident playbooks MUST address data disclosure, injection/agent compromise, poisoning, provider/model compromise, unsafe output/action, outage, and supply-chain compromise.
Model/read/write capabilities MUST have independent kill switches; provider, prompt, policy, corpus, tool, and release rollback MUST be tested.
SLOs, RTO/RPO, safe degraded mode, manual fallback, backup/restore, reconciliation, and dependency failure behavior MUST be approved for care operations.
The index MUST contain only owner-approved, malware/content-reviewed, classified, versioned, checksummed, and attributable sources.
Access control MUST execute before any sensitive chunk enters model context and MUST be rechecked after retrieval where feasible.
Retrieved/user/FHIR/tool text MUST be labeled and treated as untrusted data, never executable instruction.
Policy answers MUST use server-verifiable approved citations and source versions or explicitly abstain.
Conflicting, expired, revoked, or low-provenance sources MUST be excluded or surfaced through a defined safe conflict process.
Vector/index partitions, metadata, cache, backup, and export MUST enforce the same classification and authorization boundaries as source data.
Corpus/index versions MUST be immutable for evaluation and independently rollback-capable.
Diagnosis, prescribing, treatment recommendation, emergency triage, autonomous clinical decision/write, and patient communication MUST be blocked in v1.
Urgent/emergency language MUST trigger fixed established-channel guidance and no autonomous action; the system MUST NOT assess urgency.
The UI MUST distinguish draft/proposal/approved/executed/failed states and MUST NOT imply completion before trusted confirmation.
Patient identity, source/version, uncertainty, destination, exact action, and material changes MUST be understandable at decision points.
The supported workflow and approval MUST meet current Northstar accessibility target (at least WCAG 2.2 AA design target) with a non-AI alternative.
Safety events, near misses, complaints, overrides/edits, abstention, source defects, and subgroup performance MUST be monitored with approved stop thresholds.
Source changes MUST receive review, required tests, secret/SAST/SCA scanning, and protected-branch release gates.
Dependencies and CI actions MUST be locked or immutable-SHA pinned; build artifacts MUST have SBOM/AIBOM, provenance, vulnerability results, and signatures before promotion.
Release evaluation MUST cover function, authorization, privacy, security, safety, grounding, robustness, accessibility, performance, cost, and recovery with versioned datasets/thresholds.
Adversarial testing MUST cover direct/indirect/stored/obfuscated injection, exfiltration, poisoning, tool/identity abuse, action mutation/replay, output injection, and consumption.
A release MUST NOT proceed with an open critical/high gate blocker; accepted residual risk MUST be named, evidence-based, time-bound, monitored, and approved.
Evidence MUST be reproducible, minimal, public-safe where published, and traceable to a revision, configuration, test corpus, owner, and decision.

scope: Local synthetic-data simulation; not pilot, production, compliance certification, or clinical validation.
